families.label: Walsh characters and diagonal phase synthesis
families.question: Can a short parity expansion replace a full table of diagonal phases?
families.formula: w_j(x)=(-1)^{\langle j,x\rangle_2},\quad F_S=\sum_{j\in S}a_jW_j,\quad e^{-i\tau F_S}=\prod_{j\in S}e^{-i\tau a_jW_j}
families.mechanism: A Walsh character is a diagonal Pauli-Z string once the source's bit-reversal convention is fixed. All strings commute, so each term becomes parity computation, a Z rotation and uncomputation. This makes a short function description into a phase operator; it does not by itself prepare its amplitude state.
assumptions: Real sampled function, an explicitly supplied Walsh coefficient list and a fixed dyadic grid/bit convention
Sparsity and maximum Hamming weight are supplied or proved; differentiability is not sparsity
Retain j=0: its global phase becomes a relative phase when the operator is controlled
Approximation, coefficient computation, angle precision, connectivity and work-register cleanup are separately charged
proof_steps: Identify each diagonal entry of W_j with the source Walsh character; prove orthogonality and coefficient reconstruction under the selected ordering.
Compose parity compute–rotate–uncompute into exp(-i tau a_j W_j), including the empty parity j=0.
Use diagonal commutation to prove the product formula, then bound truncation in the specified norm.
Only after phase synthesis closes, compose a separately verified interference/postselection consumer and charge success probability.
families.boundary: Planned source formalization, not a local Walsh theorem. Existing UCRY or Python Walsh/Gray multiplexor code is not a proof of the Walsh Series Loader. Sparse Walsh support is not sparse computational-basis support.

technical_card.statement: An explicit real Walsh expansion supplies a commuting diagonal phase circuit; the controlled circuit must include its constant coefficient. The amplitude-loading consumer is a separate obligation.
technical_card.next_action: Prove a bit-order-aware single Walsh-string matrix action, with j=0 and its controlled version, before proving truncation or loader complexity.
failure_modes: Deleting a global phase before controlling the circuit changes interference.
Identifying Walsh integer order with physical little-endian wire order without the source adapter.
Inferring polynomial loading of arbitrary data from a sparse phase expansion.
Treating shared Walsh terminology as a checked reuse of the UCRY backend.

families.label: Diagonal filters, accepted branches and normalization
families.question: What does a cheap diagonal circuit really cost when used to prepare a state?
families.mechanism: A unitary diagonal changes phases but not probabilities. A non-unitary diagonal must be realized as an accepted branch of a larger unitary. Normalize only a nonzero branch, and account for repeated attempts or amplitude amplification. Walsh loading is one interference-based consumer, not identical to a general diagonal block encoding.
assumptions: Normalized input with a charged preparation/inverse supplier; total scale alpha>0 bounds max |d_x|; it equals source alpha_src times dmax
Source V.1 covers signed real D; complex D needs the separate modulus–phase extension, a zero-entry phase convention and charged phase synthesis
Chosen ancilla success sector, complex phases, register order and clean workspace are explicit
Nonzero D psi and a quantitative lower bound on its norm for efficient normalized output
Data-copy parallelism means coherent computational-basis fanout followed by uncomputation, not cloning an unknown quantum state
Exact arbitrary tables can have exponential size; approximation savings need a function-class promise
proof_steps: Specify the exact projected-block identity before discussing normalized output.
Compute the squared norm of the accepted branch and derive p; distinguish operator error from normalized-state error.
For WSL, derive the actual interference branch -i(I-exp(-i tau F_S))|+^n>/2 before the small-angle approximation.
Compile a declared sequential/parallel schedule, count workspace and cleanup, then charge all repetitions, reflections and inverses.
families.boundary: The linked cubic theorem is a fixed two-data-qubit diagonal witness, not an arbitrary-width Walsh/diagonal compiler or its complexity theorem. Small operator error alone does not control a nearly zero postselected state's error.

technical_card.statement: A diagonal block applied to a specified input yields a conditional normalized state with success ||D psi||^2/alpha^2. Space/depth/accuracy tradeoffs must be compared at matched input, error and success contracts.
technical_card.next_action: Prove the generic projected-branch probability identity using existing finite-matrix objects; keep the paper's literal dilation and circuit schedule as subsequent source obligations.
failure_modes: Quoting per-attempt depth as time to a successful prepared state.
Confusing state infidelity with vector or operator norm error, or forgetting alpha_total when converting source Eq. (18) normalized-block error to the local unscaled-operator convention.
Ignoring input-state preparation, reflections or inverse access in amplification.
Claiming a deterministic system-only non-unitary gate.
Calling a uniform-input cost bound a bound for every localized input.
Promoting the source Fig. 4 / Eqs. (19)-(21) / Appendix B signal sector before reconciling its labels.
Assuming III.2 integer rounding and VIII.1 size versus depth accounting have already been reconciled.

families.label: Finite matrices, norms and registers
families.question: Are dimensions, basis order, scalar field and selected subspace fixed?
families.mechanism: Use matrix-entry and state-action contracts before optimizing circuits. A first column and an entire projected block are different targets.
assumptions: Finite dimensions and explicit little-/big-endian conversion
Positive normalizer; selected input and output ancilla states
Named vector/operator norm and exact versus approximate tolerance
proof_steps: Name the basis equivalence and the clean projector.
Prove unitarity independently of the target action.
Evaluate all requested entries, not only a finite diagnostic subset.
families.boundary: A structure accepting a proposition is an interface, not an unconditional construction theorem.

families.label: Hermite matching and Bernstein subdivision
families.question: Does a known function admit an exact low-degree local update?
families.mechanism: Preserve the literal Hermite polynomial while changing basis. Binary interval subdivision updates a fixed-size coefficient row, rather than enumerating samples.
assumptions: Degree d=2k+1 and all endpoint jets are fixed
Subdivision coordinate and polynomial coordinate must be reconciled
Positivity on [0,1] is separate from the identity on all real coordinates
proof_steps: Match derivatives at both endpoints; uniqueness follows because the difference has 2k+2 zeros counted with multiplicity.
Expand the endpoint factors in the Bernstein basis and identify the coefficients.
Apply de Casteljau restrictions along a bit path and reconcile its coordinate with the sample index.
families.boundary: This is exact representation of the chosen polynomial, not automatic spectral convergence of a PDE solver. The general function-to-MPS idea predates ASPBE.

families.label: Bounded-memory function representations
families.question: Can each bit update a small state instead of selecting a table entry?
families.mechanism: Exponentials factor over bits; polynomial coefficients evolve in a degree-bounded space; one unresolved partition boundary is routed through a small additional state.
assumptions: Explicit cores are supplied from formulas, not selected from an existence theorem
TT rank is bounded across every chosen bit cut
Branch masks, phase information and endpoints are preserved
proof_steps: Prove each local core computes its intended bit update.
Induct on the remaining word to identify the contraction with the literal function value.
Count stored core entries and compare with a dense amplitude table.
families.boundary: Smoothness or a symbolic formula alone does not guarantee low TT rank or a cheap core supplier in arbitrary dimension.

families.label: Local Gram normalization
families.question: Can normalization be computed without summing exponentially many amplitudes?
families.mechanism: Distribute the sum of squared contractions into local matrix products; compute the same finite norm from right to left.
assumptions: Real cores in this local Hermite route; use conjugate transpose for complex cores
A nonzero raw state and compatible boundary dimensions
Core construction and finite-bit arithmetic are separately charged
proof_steps: Expand the squared scalar contraction.
Exchange finite sums and collect the two values of the next bit.
Inductively identify the Gram environment with the exact suffix norm and take the positive square root.
families.boundary: An exact-real operation count is not a bit-complexity bound or a floating-point stability theorem.

families.label: Canonicalization, completion and local compilation
families.question: Can a bounded-rank description be turned into an actual primitive list?
families.mechanism: Canonicalize without changing the contraction, absorb the signed scalar boundary, complete each local isometry, compile its actual orthogonal matrix and assemble physical wires.
assumptions: Normalized scalar-boundary real TT
Rank-deficient factors and signed boundary cases are handled
All non-clean output sectors vanish at the final stage
proof_steps: Factor local cores and pass the residual factor to the neighboring core.
Prove preservation of every contracted amplitude and the local isometry identity.
Complete to an orthogonal matrix, decompose into plane rotations and compile to RY/CX.
Compose the stages and prove both clean output and primitive resource bounds.
families.boundary: The current symbolic resource theorem does not include a full stable finite-precision T-gate compiler.

families.label: State-action and coherent preparation contracts
families.question: Is the requested object one state, a coherent family, or a mixed state?
families.mechanism: Fix all output sectors. A family also fixes relative phases between parameters; density-matrix trace error is a separate contract.
assumptions: Target normalization and nonzero source
Relative phase convention for controlled families
Success probability and garbage register behavior declared
proof_steps: Read the exact first-column predicate.
Prove each target amplitude and every non-clean sector.
For controlled families, prove a single coherent map rather than per-parameter rays.
families.boundary: Correctness up to a parameter-dependent global phase is not sufficient for a coherent family.

families.label: PREPARE–SELECT–unprepare
families.question: Are coefficient preparation and controlled operator access both available?
families.mechanism: Prepare coefficients sqrt(w_a/alpha), select the corresponding unitary, and unprepare. Phases for complex coefficients must be assigned explicitly.
assumptions: Nonnegative weights w_a and alpha=sum w_a>0, or an explicit complex-phase adapter
Implementable SELECT and adjoint PREPARE, not merely copies of a state
Compatible data/ancilla layouts and normalization
proof_steps: Expand PREPARE on the clean ancilla.
Apply SELECT branch by branch.
Contract with the same coefficient preparation to obtain weighted matrix entries.
families.boundary: SP can be a BE ingredient, but one isolated state does not determine a general matrix. This explanatory bridge has no newly certified transport root.

families.label: Block extraction and spectral filtering
families.question: What norm, overlap and polynomial approximation determine success?
families.mechanism: A projected block supplies an unnormalized desired branch. Normalize conditionally and explicitly account for amplification and polynomial-approximation errors.
assumptions: A nonzero accepted branch
Known normalization alpha and available inverses/controls as used
Gap/overlap or filling assumptions for efficiency, not for mere definition
proof_steps: Apply the clean projection to identify the accepted branch.
Use Born's rule to derive its norm-squared probability.
Bound approximation and success amplification under the declared access model.
families.boundary: Block encoding does not make normalized state preparation deterministic or uniformly cheap.

families.label: Fourier multipliers and Schrödingerisation
families.question: Can a nonunitary evolution be represented as transport in an auxiliary coordinate?
families.mechanism: A Fourier basis converts transport into a real-frequency Hermitian multiplier. Smooth extension improves a separate approximation problem; its sampled preparation is a reusable input supplier.
assumptions: A_1 and A_2 Hermitian with declared Fourier sign and register order
Domain/boundary or finite discretization fixed
Safe recovery region and truncation error are explicit
proof_steps: Split A into its Hermitian and anti-Hermitian parts.
Differentiate the warped profile on its recovery region.
Specify the Fourier transform and identify the derivative multiplier.
Separate initial-state, discretization, simulation and recovery errors.
families.boundary: This is a candidate mathematical route, not an end-to-end PDE theorem inferred from Hermite state preparation.

families.label: Envelopes and coherent rejection
families.question: Is a reference state closer to the target than the uniform state in a controllable sense?
families.mechanism: Prepare g, apply a controlled contraction f/(Cg) on its support, and retain the success branch. Costs of g, the ratio and amplification must all be paid.
assumptions: support(f) subset support(g), with f/g defined as zero off support(g)
C>0, nonzero f and g, and a verified pointwise domination bound
Magnitude and complex phase of the ratio implemented coherently
proof_steps: Write the reference amplitude as g_j/||g||.
Multiply the accepted branch by f_j/(C g_j); the g_j factor cancels on support.
Sum squared accepted amplitudes to obtain success probability, then normalize.
families.boundary: Changing from probability sampling to amplitudes requires square roots and phase handling. An envelope with small kappa is not automatically easy to prepare.

families.label: Charged access and finite-precision compilation
families.question: Does a query or symbolic gate hide the dominant work?
families.formula: T_{\rm total}=T_{\rm preprocessing}+Q\,T_{\rm oracle}+T_{\rm synthesis}+T_{\rm readout}
families.mechanism: Separate descriptions, arithmetic operations, bit operations, logical rotations, T/Toffoli gates, depth, connectivity and ancillas. Compare only matching models.
assumptions: Input encoding and precision specified
One cost model for both upper and lower bounds
Initialization, maintenance, amplification and measurements charged
proof_steps: Freeze the access model before optimizing.
Bind costs to actual data producers and primitive lists.
Budget each numerical error and then sum compositional errors.
families.boundary: The local norm theorem is only a substrate. It is not the entire displayed end-to-end cost decomposition certified in Lean.

families.label: Gibbs invariance versus mixing
families.question: Does the generator only preserve the target, or converge to it with a useful rate?
families.mechanism: Connect invariance, reversibility/detailed balance, coercivity and error contraction only through explicit model-specific hypotheses.
assumptions: Specified Hamiltonian, temperature and target state
Primitive semigroup and quantitative convergence assumptions when used
Implementation and mixing error separated
proof_steps: Prove the invariant-state equation.
Identify the quantitative coercivity/mixing certificate still missing.
Compose convergence with implemented-channel error.
families.boundary: This is a conceptual connection to Samplinglib, not a transfer of classical LSI results to arbitrary quantum generators.

families.label: Structure-aware preparation and verification
families.question: Can the preparation structure supply a cheap experimental witness?
families.mechanism: Keep kernel-checked ideal-circuit equality separate from noisy-hardware fidelity estimation. A structural witness needs an explicit measurement and sample-complexity theorem.
assumptions: Measurement access and noise model stated
IID or non-IID assumptions explicit
Confidence level, sample count and target description cost charged
proof_steps: State the ideal target and the observed channel separately.
Derive an observable or witness for the chosen state class.
Bound estimation error and confidence under the measurement assumptions.
families.boundary: The candidate hardware paper is not primary-verified here; no reported numerical performance is used as a proved bound.

hyperedges.label: Walsh phases + interference + nonzero branch
hyperedges.mechanism: Combine a controlled diagonal phase supplier with ancilla interference, postselection and a normalized-error theorem.
hyperedges.hypothesis_map: Real function, source bit order, supplied coefficients, retained zero mode, explicit input and inverse access, small-angle/truncation bounds and nonzero accepted branch.
hyperedges.conclusion_map: An approximate amplitude state with a declared infidelity and success-dependent total cost, not an unconditional n-independent loader.
hyperedges.failure_boundary: Constant-term removal changes the controlled circuit; small filling fraction or poor sparsity can remove the advantage.
hyperedges.review: Source-planning edge; independent conceptual review pending; no local transport theorem

hyperedges.label: Diagonal block + prepared input + success contract
hyperedges.mechanism: Specialize the existing BE-to-SP consumer to a diagonal filter; retain input preparation and successful-branch normalization as AND inputs.
hyperedges.hypothesis_map: Literal source dilation, bounded diagonal, known success sector, nonzero output, charged inverse/control and matched error metric.
hyperedges.conclusion_map: A conditional state and model-specific space–depth–accuracy/resource comparison.
hyperedges.failure_boundary: Neither a diagonal function description nor a compiled nearby fixed-size example certifies a scalable supplier; this is not SP-to-BE inclusion.
hyperedges.review: Source-planning edge; independent conceptual review pending; no local transport theorem

hyperedges.label: Exact function structure to bounded memory
hyperedges.mechanism: Keep local polynomial updates and branch routing together; neither alone proves the sampled source.
hyperedges.hypothesis_map: Endpoint jets, grid coordinate, boundary ownership and bit order agree.
hyperedges.conclusion_map: The finite core contraction equals the literal sampled Hermite function.
hyperedges.failure_boundary: A degree statement alone does not account for an arbitrary number of pieces.
hyperedges.review: independent conceptual review pending; local Lean roots have their own build evidence

hyperedges.label: Normalize AND compile AND clean
hyperedges.mechanism: Compose the source, norm and primitive-circuit interfaces.
hyperedges.hypothesis_map: Real normalized scalar-boundary chain, rank bound, padded register layout and signed residual boundary.
hyperedges.conclusion_map: All target amplitudes and all non-clean sectors, plus actual primitive-list count.
hyperedges.failure_boundary: An existence-only TT representation or unknown normalizer is not a data-producing compiler.
hyperedges.review: independent conceptual review pending; not a certified functor

hyperedges.label: SP + SELECT gives an LCU block
hyperedges.mechanism: The AND node explicitly includes controlled operator access and unpreparation.
hyperedges.hypothesis_map: Square-root coefficient amplitudes, SELECT unitaries, adjoint access and phase convention.
hyperedges.conclusion_map: A specified projected matrix block, not merely one state.
hyperedges.failure_boundary: No arrow from an isolated prepared state to arbitrary A; state copies do not supply controlled U or U-dagger.

hyperedges.label: BE + input + overlap gives a state branch
hyperedges.mechanism: Project the block, retain the accepted branch and account for success amplification.
hyperedges.hypothesis_map: Nonzero A psi, available input preparation and declared oracle inverses/controls.
hyperedges.conclusion_map: Normalized A psi conditional on success or an explicitly amplified approximation.
hyperedges.failure_boundary: Small overlap can dominate the cost; this is not an unconditional cheap reverse conversion.

hyperedges.label: Harmonic analysis to quantum evolution
hyperedges.mechanism: The prepared auxiliary profile is one supplier; operator access and recovery remain separate.
hyperedges.hypothesis_map: Hermitian components, Fourier sign, finite grid and norm/recovery budget.
hyperedges.failure_boundary: SP certification alone proves neither the Hamiltonian block encoding nor end-to-end PDE accuracy.

hyperedges.label: Sampling envelope meets function structure
hyperedges.mechanism: Search for an envelope with both a provable ratio bound and a constructive small representation.
hyperedges.hypothesis_map: Support domination, ratio degree/rank, phase access and charged reference preparation.
hyperedges.conclusion_map: A model-specific success and end-to-end cost target.
hyperedges.failure_boundary: A good classical envelope need not have a cheap coherent preparation; no universal cure for dimensionality.

hyperedges.label: A coercivity mechanism, not an equality of samplers
hyperedges.mechanism: Compare the role of a functional inequality in classical and quantum semigroups.
hyperedges.hypothesis_map: Different state spaces, noncommutativity, detailed-balance conventions and divergences remain explicit.
hyperedges.conclusion_map: A hypothesis-mapped conceptual mirror with candidate shared matrix/semigroup lemmas.
hyperedges.failure_boundary: Classical LSI or reversibility is not automatically a quantum KMS mixing certificate.

hyperedges.label: Preparation structure plus measurement contract
hyperedges.mechanism: Use the state description to propose a measurement witness; formal circuit proof and statistical evidence remain separate.
hyperedges.hypothesis_map: Experimental measurement access, noise, sample model, epsilon and delta.
hyperedges.conclusion_map: Candidate low-sample verification protocol for a specified family.
hyperedges.failure_boundary: An ideal Lean proof is not a hardware fidelity certificate.

contributions.label: Hermite: dense tree to bounded-memory construction
contributions.head: d638f725b7ed07fc471c25730cdf3bcfebe00510
contributions.before: Generic amplitude tree retains one independent branch per sample; exponential gate count in the data-qubit count, not exponential ancillas.
contributions.after: Preserve the formula through Bernstein subdivision and bounded TT cores, then reuse a generic local-isometry compiler.
contributions.invariant: Same discrete normalized Hermite state and clean-output convention; exact-real primitive gate model.
contributions.novelty_boundary: Curated repository contribution. Function-to-MPS and sequential preparation are prior art; the metadata does not certify global novelty, optimality or a finite-bit speedup.
